channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro: 'Presidente da República deixa legado de incompetência e corrupção'
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL candidate, criticized the current president, claiming his administration leaves a legacy of incompetence and corruption. Speaking at his campaign launch in Copacabana, he said he will not give up on Brazil and lamented that his father, Jair Bolsonaro, cannot attend due to being 'hated' by some powerful groups.

item.title: Em largada, Lula foca em mulheres, e Flávio defende pai e fala de segurança
item.description: Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), the two candidates leading in presidential election polls, launched their campaigns today in their respective political strongholds. Lula focused his message on appealing to women voters, while Flávio Bolsonaro defended his father Jair Bolsonaro's image and emphasized public security as a central pillar of his campaign.

item.title: Cartão corporativo sigiloso do Planalto já registra mais de R$ 8,5 milhões em gastos no ano
item.description: A confidential corporate card of the Presidency of the Republic has recorded over R$8.5 million in expenses in 2025, according to updated government data. These cards, used by officials under secrecy, are typically linked to the president or sensitive security sectors of the Planalto Palace. The lack of transparency prevents identifying the specific expenses incurred with these funds.

item.title: Eleições 2026: veja a agenda de Lenilda Luna neste domingo (16)
item.description: Lenilda Luna, the UP candidate for Governor of Alagoas, launches her electoral campaign this Sunday (16) with an event in the Vergel do Lago neighborhood of Maceió at 4 PM. The gathering will include families organized by the MLB and her running mate, Jardel Queiroz, also from the UP. Electoral campaigning is now permitted as of this date, per the TSE calendar, and will continue until October 3.

item.title: Lula critica decisão de Toffoli que impediu ele de ir ao enterro de irmão
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) criticized Minister Dias Toffoli of the STF for authorizing his release from prison in 2019 only to meet with family in a military unit, but not in time to attend his brother Vavá’s funeral. Speaking in São Bernardo do Campo, Lula contrasted this with the permission he received during the military dictatorship to attend his mother’s funeral, emphasizing the irony that a democratically appointed judge denied him the same right. The speech marked the launch of his 2026 electoral campaign, returning to his union roots in the ABC region.

item.title: Ato de campanha no ABC enaltece história de Lula, mas aponta pouco para o futuro
item.description: Lula's campaign kickoff in São Bernardo do Campo emphasized his historical legacy, invoking past struggles and allies, with limited focus on future proposals. Although he mentioned the potential creation of a public security ministry contingent on congressional approval of the PEC da Segurança, the speech was dominated by nostalgia and comparisons to Bolsonaro's administration, leaving his plans for a fourth term unclear.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro disputam as ruas no 1º dia da campanha; veja como foram os atos
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro launched their presidential campaigns with symbolic street acts in São Bernardo do Campo and Rio de Janeiro, respectively, highlighting the battle for public space on the first day. Lula spoke to thousands of supporters at the Primeiro de Maio stadium, a historic site of his union past, while Flávio addressed crowds from a sound truck on Avenida Atlântica. Other candidates, including Renan Santos, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema, held events in various regions across Brazil.

item.title: Flávio invoca pai e Lula apela para soberania em atos inaugurais de campanha
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro launched their presidential campaigns with contrasting events: Lula, in São Bernardo do Campo, emphasized national sovereignty, labor policies, and class struggle, invoking his union past and advocating for the Public Security PEC. Flávio, in Copacabana, evoked the memory of his father, Jair Bolsonaro, and highlighted support for conservative agendas, using a symbolic location of bolsonarism.

item.title: Flávio fala com Ramagem pelo canal 'Timeline' antes do início de sua campanha
item.description: Before officially launching his electoral campaign on Copacabana Beach, PL candidate Flávio Bolsonaro gave a brief interview to the 'Timeline' channel and interacted with Alexandre Ramagem. The conversation took place this Sunday and foreshadowed the themes of his candidacy.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro contrapõe discurso de soberania de Lula e mira segurança
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a presidential candidate, linked sovereignty and public security in his first campaign act in Rio de Janeiro, criticizing President Lula (PT). He framed security as a pillar of national sovereignty, contrasting it with what he perceives as the current government's failures in combating crime.

item.title: “Vou ser o próximo presidente”, diz Flávio em 1º ato de campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) launched his presidential campaign with an event at Copacabana Beach in Rio de Janeiro, declaring he intends to become the next president by confronting the 'system'. In his speech, he criticized institutional actions and reiterated his opposition to the political establishment.

item.title: Ruas inicia campanha falando em 'novo tempo' para o Rio, mas recebe pouco espaço durante ato bolsonarista em Copacabana
item.description: Douglas Ruas (PL) said he could 'inaugurate a new time for Rio de Janeiro' during a Bolsonarist rally in Copacabana, but was given little speaking time, delivering his remarks only at 12:23 after brief mentions by allies. His campaign emphasized that the official launch will occur on the 22nd at Maracanãzinho, while facing the challenge of gaining voter recognition amid Eduardo Paes (PSD)'s lead, who holds 38% voting intention compared to Ruas' 10% in the July 27 Quaest poll.

item.title: Tarcísio fala em "falsa comunicação de crime" de motorista de Haddad
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas stated that analysis of over 70 cameras and GPS data indicates false crime reporting by Fernando Haddad's driver, denying any police stop. He said the driver will be summoned to testify and could face criminal charges if false reporting is confirmed. Haddad had claimed he was intimidated by a PM vehicle with visible rifles, a claim the SSP rejected after preliminary investigation.

item.title: ‘No governo passado, Mercedes-Benz e Ford fecharam. Hoje, temos GWM e BYD’, diz Alckmin
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) highlighted the revival of automotive production in Brazil under President Lula’s government, noting that factories closed during the Bolsonaro era — such as Mercedes-Benz in Iracemápolis and Ford in Bahia — have been replaced by GWM and BYD. He also cited export growth, Mercosul trade agreements with Singapore, EFTA, and the European Union, along with progress in employment, income, GDP, and social investments.

item.title: Com falas antigas de Jair, Flávio apela para memória do pai preso em primeiro ato de campanha
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro launched his 2026 election campaign in Copacabana, invoking his father Jair Bolsonaro’s legacy through old audio clips, bolsonarist slogans, and emotional appeals like 'Come back, Bolsonaro'. He positioned himself as the political heir, pledging to appoint four STF justices aligned with conservative values and claiming his family prevents Brazil from becoming a dictatorship.

item.title: Haddad lança campanha ao governo de SP em comício de Lula em São Bernardo do Campo
item.description: Fernando Haddad launched his campaign for governor of São Paulo during Lula’s rally in São Bernardo do Campo, selecting the symbolic site of the president’s union origins to kick off the electoral race. In his speech, Haddad praised Lula’s political trajectory, highlighting economic growth, SUS strengthening, and expanded access to higher education through Prouni and FIES, while emphasizing his own humble background and close ties to Lula as a former minister.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vai a São Januário para assistir a Vasco x Santos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, a 2026 presidential candidate, is set to attend the Vasco vs. Santos match at Estádio São Januário this Sunday, following a formal invitation from the club. The Federal Police informed Vasco of his presence, and Santos striker Neymar is also confirmed to play. Vasco emphasized its political neutrality, stating the invitation is strictly operational for safety and logistics, not an endorsement, and has been extended equally to all presidential candidates.

item.title: Ato de Lula mira Congresso e afaga mulheres e evangélicos
item.description: Lula launched his re-election campaign in São Bernardo do Campo, promising to create a Ministry of Public Security, expand his congressional base, and appeal to women and evangelicals. His speech was more concise than at the PT convention, addressing education reform and criticizing Bolsonaro’s alleged loosening of gun laws. Lula stressed that the new ministry depends on securing a stronger legislative majority in the election.

item.title: TSE determina remoção de vídeo que associa Lula ao PCC e ao CV
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ruled by a five-to-two vote to remove a video posted by Flávio Bolsonaro that falsely associates President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva with the PCC and CV criminal factions, classifying it as premature electoral propaganda and defamation. The court also ordered social media platform X to take down the post. A separate request by Minister André Mendonça to obtain internal documents from the Brazil of Hope Federation was denied due to procedural irregularities in case distribution.

item.title: Integrante do Novo aciona TSE contra candidatura de Pablo Marçal
item.description: Federal deputy candidate Santana Pires (GO-Novo) filed a challenge with the TSE against Pablo Marçal’s presidential candidacy, arguing Marçal remains ineligible until 2032 due to a São Paulo Electoral Court ruling. He contests the timing of Marçal’s candidacy registration (claiming it was submitted after the deadline), the absence of policy proposals in the registration documents, and the legitimacy of Marçal’s PRTB affiliation, citing a court decision that regularized the membership retroactively only for procedural purposes. Santana also urges the TSE to refer the matter to the Public Prosecutor’s Office to investigate potential fraud in party affiliations involving PRTB president Leonardo Avalanche.

item.title: “O barbudo tem o STF e o dinheiro da corrupção”, diz Alfredo Gaspar
item.description: Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), vice-presidential candidate, claimed that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, referred to as 'the bearded one', controls the Supreme Court, corruption money, and has imprisoned supporters applauding him, while presenting Flávio Bolsonaro as the hope of Brazil's 'decent people'. The statement was made during Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign launch at Copacabana Beach, RJ, where Gaspar also noted that former President Jair Bolsonaro faced assassination attempts and family separation, but Brazil will raise its green and yellow flags again.

item.title: Ato de Flávio Bolsonaro em Copacabana começa com espaços vazios
item.description: The first campaign event of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), presidential candidate, took place on Copacabana Beach on Sunday (Aug 16, 2026) with visible empty spaces, suggesting low initial attendance. The gathering occurred near Post 5, in his hometown and the Bolsonaro family’s electoral stronghold. A live stream was provided for viewers to follow the event.

item.title: Lula arranca la campaña para conquistar un cuarto mandato: “No voy a permitir que la derecha regrese al poder”
item.description: Lula launched his seventh electoral campaign at the same union hall where he led worker strikes during Brazil's dictatorship, seeking a fourth presidential term. In an impassioned speech, he vowed to prevent the right from returning to power, blaming it for 400,000 Covid deaths due to irresponsibility and calling for investment in education, health, and jobs.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro fará campanha com colete à prova de balas, diz líder do PL
item.description: The leader of the PL party in the Chamber of Deputies, Sóstenes Cavalcante, stated that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL’s presidential candidate for 2026, will conduct his entire campaign wearing a bulletproof vest. The remark highlights the heightened climate of tension and insecurity in Brazilian politics, particularly among right-wing figures.

item.title: Michelle: “Vamos eleger Flávio Bolsonaro presidente”
item.description: Former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro (PL), running for Senate in the Federal District, urged voters to support Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), the presidential candidate, during campaign events in Brasília and Ceilândia. She appeared alongside Governor Celina Leão (PP), who is running for re-election, and advocated for Flávio Bolsonaro to become Brazil's next president.

item.title: Lulistas cobram governo por concessão de prédio histórico no Rio
item.description: Supporters of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva are demanding the federal government grant concession of the Casarão Cândido Mendes building in Rio de Janeiro’s Santa Teresa neighborhood, currently occupied by 64 families since 1997. Although the property was approved for the Minha Casa, Minha Vida – Entidades program in June 2026, the concession has not been granted, blocking renovation and social work efforts. The activists sold custom shirts during Lula’s re-election campaign launch in São Bernardo do Campo, urging the president to intervene directly.

item.title: Tarcísio inicia campanha em Osasco com presença de 14 prefeitos e lideranças partidárias
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) launched his re-election campaign in Osasco, an event that also served as the launch for Rogério Lins (Podemos) as a state deputy candidate. The gathering featured 14 mayors, including São Paulo's Ricardo Nunes (MDB), and leaders from 10 allied parties, showcasing political strength. Tarcísio promised local improvements such as a Fire Department, integration with Poupatempo, a Bom Prato meal program, progress on Metro Line 22, and a specialized medical outpatient clinic in Osasco.

item.title: Vila Euclides fica com espaços vazios na largada de Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva officially launched his 2026 re-election campaign at the Estádio Municipal 1º de Maio in São Bernardo do Campo, the historic Vila Euclides site. Despite the venue's significance as a labor movement stronghold, aerial footage revealed under-attendance, with empty sections caused by large banners and obstructed views behind the stage.

item.title: Lula dá pontapé inicial na campanha usando as cores do Brasil e falando em soberania nacional
item.description: President Lula kicked off his re-election campaign at an event in the Vila Euclides Stadium in São Bernardo do Campo, emphasizing national sovereignty, public safety, women's protection, rare earth exploration, education valorization, and the need to elect workers' representatives over business owners. The event featured the Brazilian flag, a rendition of the national anthem by Fafá de Belém, and green and yellow fireworks. Lula blamed the Bolsonaro government for pandemic deaths, denounced organized crime operating from affluent areas, and called for constitutional changes to strengthen security and education, framing his vision as a class-based struggle against elite interests.

item.title: Lula discursa em primeiro dia de campanha; veja principais frases
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) delivered his first campaign speech for the 2026 election in São Bernardo do Campo (SP), criticizing the right and proposing policies on public security, full-time education, and critical mineral exploration. The speech took place in the city where Lula began his political career in the 1970s union movement, marking the official start of the campaign, which now allows explicit vote requests, rallies, and online advertising. TV and radio advertising will only be permitted starting August 28.

item.title: Em 1º ato, Lula ataca a direita, defende terras raras e fala em eleger maioria no Congresso
item.description: In his first campaign act at Vila Euclides Stadium in São Bernardo do Campo, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) attacked the right, accusing it of responsibility for 400,000 COVID deaths and mocking children lacking medicine. He defended Brazil’s exploration of rare earth minerals and stressed the need to elect a favorable majority in Congress to advance his agenda. The event marked the launch of his 2026 re-election campaign, highlighting his union roots and vowing to keep fighting as long as he lives.

item.title: Lula lança campanha de chapéu e com vídeo para Lula de 1979
item.description: Lula launched his re-election campaign in São Bernardo do Campo, wearing a hat due to radiotherapy for skin cancer, and emphasized the importance of respecting women and ending gender-based violence. He also presented a video in which he read a letter written to himself in 1979, reflecting on his union and political trajectory. Fernando Haddad, candidate for governor of São Paulo, stated that Lula 'put inflation on its knees' for the second time and credited the government with economic growth, job recovery, and expansion of public education.

item.title: Janja: “Antes de casar com um Silva, eu já era uma Silva”
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva stated she already bore the Silva surname before marrying President Lula, using her personal story to advocate for women's participation in politics and society. She emphasized that women hold multiple roles and that individual progress lifts all women, noting the PT's increased inclusion of women in the campaign launch after a national convention oversight. Janja also publicly mentioned Lula's former wife, Marisa Letícia, for the first time, crediting her with embroidering the PT's first flag.

item.title: ‘Subir junto a rampa do Palácio’: Flávio e Ramagem conversam antes do início da campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro gave an interview before officially launching his campaign at Copacabana beach, stating his candidacy is a 'purpose of God' and that he aims to assume power in 2027 to bring back political exiles like Alexandre Ramagem and Eduardo Bolsonaro, citing what he called 'leftist political persecution'. Ramagem, a fugitive in the U.S. after being convicted for attempted coup, congratulated him via video call, saying he is 'more than prepared' and that they will together ascend the ramp of the Palace in 2027.

item.title: Vitória x Botafogo no Brasileirão: onde assistir, horário e escalações
item.description: Vitória and Botafogo face off this Sunday, August 16, at 6:30 PM Brasília time, at Barradão, in the 23rd round of the Brasileirão. Vitória sits 13th with 26 points, while Botafogo is ninth with 30 points despite a 6-1 loss to Cienciano in the Copa Sudamericana. The match will be exclusively broadcast on Premiere, with probable lineups already released.

item.title: Sem Kassab, Caiado lança campanha em carreata e diz que fala sobre Centrão foi mal interpretada
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado launched his electoral campaign with a motorcade in Águas Lindas de Goiás, without the presence of his running mate, Gilberto Kassab, who did not attend the event. Caiado stated that his remarks about the Centrão were misinterpreted, seeking to clarify potential political misunderstandings.

item.title: Tarcísio relembra vitória na abertura da campanha e diz: 'Osasco precisa de mais atenção'
item.description: Governor of São Paulo Tarcísio de Freitas launched his re-election campaign in Osasco, in the metropolitan region, recalling his 2022 victory and stating that the city needs more attention. He used the occasion to reinforce his initial legacy and signal priorities for a potential second term.

item.title: Centrão abandona Flávio e deixa PL com palanque esquálido no RJ e em MG
item.description: The Centrão is withdrawing regional alliances with the PL, leaving Flávio Bolsonaro with a weakened political base in Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais. According to analysis by Thais Bilenky and José Roberto de Toledo in A Hora, on UOL Canal, this fragmentation diminishes the candidate’s electoral prospects in key states for the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Caiado: 'Os Estados Unidos não mandam no Brasil; eleição nossa é no Brasil'
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado stated that the United States does not dictate Brazil's affairs and that the Brazilian election will be decided solely within the country, in response to questions about U.S.-Brazil relations.

item.title: Pazuello acena ao eleitorado feminino em primeiro ato da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Former Health Minister Eduardo Pazuello (PL) opened the campaign launch event for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the 2026 presidential race with an appeal to female voters, emphasizing health and family well-being. The event marked the official start of Flávio Bolsonaro’s candidacy, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, backed by key figures of the bolsonarist movement.

item.title: Lula reencontra metalúrgicos do ABC no lançamento de sua campanha
item.description: Lula launched his 2026 re-election campaign at Estádio 1º de Maio in São Bernardo do Campo, reuniting with ABC metalworkers and recalling his union leadership in the 1970s and 1980s. The event emphasized the history of labor strikes, the fight for democracy during the dictatorship, and the PT’s roots in social and union movements, reinforcing ties to the party’s historical base.

item.title: Advogado de Heleno desiste de candidatura após denúncia de violência doméstica
item.description: Lawyer Matheus Mayer Milanez, former federal deputy candidate for the Republicans in the Federal District, withdrew his candidacy after a protective measure was granted by the court to his ex-fiancée, who is 10 weeks pregnant and accuses him of domestic violence. The withdrawal was filed with the TSE on Friday, the 14th, two days after the court's decision.

item.title: Marina diz que não é justo oposição voltar para destruir Amazônia
item.description: Marina Silva (Rede), Senate candidate for São Paulo, stated during Lula’s re-election campaign launch that it is unfair for the opposition to return to power to destroy the Amazon and reverse social progress. She advocated for job creation, protection of women, children, and youth, and emphasized democracy and national sovereignty. Simone Tebet was also named as a Senate candidate for São Paulo, supporting the election of both women to the two available seats.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio minimizam público reduzido no ato em Copacabana
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro downplayed the low turnout at his presidential campaign kickoff in Copacabana, stating it was a political rally, not a mass demonstration, and that no buses were needed to mobilize supporters. They also justified the absence of national PL leaders such as Michelle Bolsonaro, Tarcísio de Freitas, and Nikolas Ferreira, arguing that Tarcísio’s absence from the Rio event would be 'bad' for his re-election bid in São Paulo in 2026.

item.title: Antes de ato em SP, Lula fez sessão de radioterapia para tratar câncer de pele
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva held his first campaign rally in São Bernardo do Campo (SP), revealing he had undergone a radiotherapy session to treat scalp skin cancer before the event. He explained the treatment followed the removal of a basal cell carcinoma lesion in April and that he must avoid sun exposure on his head. The rally marked the official launch of the Lula-Alckmin ticket, backed by seven parties, and took place at the site where he began his political career as a metalworker.

item.title: Pablo Marçal declara 7 bilhões em bens à Justiça Eleitoral
item.description: Pablo Marçal declared to the Electoral Justice assets worth 7.4 billion reais, a 4,276% increase from the 169.5 million reais he declared in 2024, potentially making him the wealthiest presidential candidate in Brazilian history. His candidacy was filed at the deadline following an injunction allowing his party switch from União Brasil to PRTB, though he remains ineligible until 2032 due to convictions for economic power abuse in the 2024 election.

item.title: Michelle pede votos para Flávio e diz que "logo" Bolsonaro voltará
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro urges support for Flávio Bolsonaro, who is running for president, and says Jair Bolsonaro 'will soon' return. The event took place in Ceilândia, Federal District, alongside Governor Celina Leão, emphasizing the unity of the ticket and describing her Senate campaign as a mission entrusted by the former president.

item.title: Michelle e Malafaia não comparecem a ato de Flávio, em Copacabana
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro and pastor Silas Malafaia did not attend the launch event for Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign in Copacabana, although allies claim past tensions have been resolved. Michelle, a Senate candidate for the Federal District, was focused on her own campaign and had recorded election ads with Flávio. Malafaia, a supporter of Tarcísio de Freitas, said he does not participate in partisan political acts and sent only an audio message.

item.title: Janja homenageia Marisa Letícia em 1º ato de campanha de Lula
item.description: First Lady Janja da Silva paid tribute to Marisa Letícia, Lula’s former wife, during the first campaign event for the president’s re-election bid in São Bernardo do Campo on Sunday, the 16th. The tribute underscored Marisa Letícia’s historical significance as part of the launch of Lula’s 2026 re-election campaign.

item.title: Janja cita Marisa, que foi mulher de Lula, pela 1ª vez em discurso
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva mentioned Marisa Letícia, Lula's second wife, for the first time in a public speech during the launch of the president's re-election campaign in São Bernardo do Campo. She emphasized Marisa's essential role alongside other women in the behind-the-scenes support of 1970s labor movements, including sewing the first PT flag, and criticized the historical erasure of such female contributions. The reference marks a shift from Lula's prior pattern of avoiding public mentions of Marisa since her death in 2017.
